author: dapplion
content: First I want to appreciate and celebrate your work all the zk teams work. I's absolutely crazy what has been achieved in such a short amount of time

author: dapplion
content: In your opinion and thinking ambitiously / long term, what's left to make eip8025 sound?

author: dapplion
content: Without recursion, a node that checkpoint syncs can't easily check validity of the payloads prior to the initial checkpoint sync block. CL clients are built on the assumption that ELs do that in the background with optimistic sync. Changing this would be a quite big refactor. This is a strong argument for recursive IMO

author: dapplion
content: Zisk team claims that the can easily do recursion today with 200ms of added latency and it's something they want anyway for the other systems using their proofs (rollups)

author: dapplion
content: Without recursion we need to implement proof sync in Lighthouse, which is a significant effort of ~5k lines, plus having to persist proofs bloating storage (retention window x supported proofs types (say 4) x ~0.25-1MiB = 7-29 GB / day based on retention period

author: jsign
content:
- Proof recursion, since today's 8025 doesn't have a scalable way to sync up nodes. The amount of bandwidth require to pull individual proofs is too big. (i.e. mainly what you're focusing on this convo).
- The above has implications for zkVMs to support recursive proofs. Yes, Zisk has this; but isn't clear for others and not yet part of the standards. (Although we can do it).
- Recursive proving  requires even more performance measurements since the 2-out-3 policy requires a much tighter proving time for every 3 candidates. Also, this means provers **must** also generate the 3 proofs, even if they 99% of hte time propagate 2. The third one shoudl be as performant as the two fastest. You can't avoid proving the slowest one since the recursion forces you to always have the prevous one even if you only use it 0.01% of the time.
- A network reorg has also implications on how a prover can recover from proof creation, since now they might need to create a new chain of proofs for 3 guest/zkvms in a short amount of time.

Leaving aside recursion:
- Some opcodes and precompiles in the EL layer need repricing, since there are tail-risk prover killers that we know are possible. So we need another EIP to do proper repricing such as worst-case blocks won't halt the network liveness.
- We have to as much FV as possible in zkVMs and guest programs, since attestors will rely on 2-out-3 proofs. Soundness is critical since most of the network will be attesting using those.
- We have to double-check if we need prover incentives, or can be consider a cost paid by block rewards + MEV. Not clear yet. 
- We have to see if L1 keeps pushing the gas limit and this fits the low-ish hw requirements we want for provers.

author: jsign
content:
Most of these things are more on the "Mandatory proof" box in the strawmap. 8025 is mainly about a million other things that don't depend on solving those problems, and upstreaming the work safely to CL, ELs, and specs.

If not, we leave absolutely everything to "Mandatory proofs" and is a huge EIP with a lot of risk and work to maintain until then, when we know a lot of engineering things are already mature and safe to upstream.
